Agent limitations

Supports baseline, original Learn and compatible policy comparison. Separate reference-context and completion research studies are not supported.

Adapter v2 is a separate agent from v1 (the same smolagents code): it shows each observation it hands to the agent as a short label (obs-1, obs-2, …, numbered in the order the agent first sees them; an observation it never sees gets no label), decodes the labels it showed back to the real IDs, and on the final turn offers only final_answer with a structured final-report format. Its results are never pooled with adapter v1.

Agent roles (the reference Actor and the native smolagents adapters) keep rule v1: at most one blind retry of the identical request, only when no answer arrived (a connection error, a timeout, or HTTP 503 after a one-second wait). FaultLab's own lab roles in this Learn campaign (Explorer discovery and challenge selections, Mechanic diagnosis and candidate requests) may re-send the identical request up to 3 times, after waits of 5 s, 20 s and 60 s, only when no answer arrived (connection error, timeout, HTTP 503), and at most 12 times in the whole campaign; during discovery the declared Explorer retry bound also applies. An answer, even an empty or malformed one, is never retried, and neither is any other HTTP status or an authentication, configuration or model-identity failure. Every retry is charged in model calls, tokens and dollars before it is sent, from unreserved campaign capacity only. A Stop during a wait ends the campaign STOPPED and nothing more is sent. If every allowed retry fails, the campaign ends ERROR as before and says how many retries were tried. Separate studies started on the campaign keep rule v1.

Exact rule text

faultlab-mechanic-context/v2-bounded: When a Mechanic candidate request (or diagnosis request) would exceed the 32,000-token model input limit, FaultLab compacts only the evidence tables it carries, in fixed stages, stopping at the first stage after which the request is at most 28,000 tokens (4,000 tokens stay free for its one format-repair turn): (1) a clean episode (no failed check, not the source or one of its reproductions) whose rows and outcome repeat an earlier clean episode is listed by episode_id instead of repeated; (2) one clean episode is kept in full per recipe, arm and trial outcome; (3) no clean episode is kept in full. The source, its reproductions and every episode with a failed check are always kept in full, and every omitted episode is still named in the request with its own outcome. The request states what was compacted and how many rows were omitted. If it still does not fit, nothing is sent and the candidate search for that source ends with a recorded reason; the campaign continues, or ends NO_CHANGE, by the existing rules. An unsent request does not use one of the campaign's candidate requests. A request that fits is sent unchanged.

faultlab-challenge-selection/v2-candidate-reach: Before a challenge pick runs any pair, FaultLab checks every fault target (tool and service) against the calls the agent under test itself made in the candidate arm's source-validation episodes of this campaign. A pick with a target the agent never called there is refused: no episode runs, and the refusal is recorded with its reason. The candidate policy's own hook reads are not agent calls. The Explorer's next request in the same challenge is a re-plan told why (one re-plan per refused pick; a refused re-plan gets none). Every request, re-plans included, is one of the challenge's existing 8 Explorer requests, charged and bounded exactly as before. The challenge itself is unchanged: 4 schedules, 3 fresh pairs each, every pair must fire its faults, and any candidate violation is a counterexample. If the candidate arm has no source-validation episode, no pick is refused.
